problems: The blind guess ('abstract thin blue strokes, no clear object') does not match the Lantern Boat. At a glance the figure is not recognisable as a boat.

The gold lines form a zigzag polyline from the stern at about (85,265) through the deck, mast and sail to the pennant at about (326,181). They read as a connect-the-dots path, not a hull, mast and sail silhouette.
The hull is a thin blue wavy line at about y=270-290, below the gold chain. It reads as water or a ripple, not a boat hull, and the keel star is not inside any closed hull outline.
The sail is not a shape. The sail head, belly and clew stars are joined by straight segments with no filled or curved sail body, so 'belly held full by the wind' is not visible.

Labels collide: 'masthead', 'sail head' and 'belly of the sail' overlap around (170-310, 210-225), and 'stern of the hull', 'keel' and 'bow end of the deck' overlap around (90-230, 245-262). The text is unreadable.
The pennant is a single thin gold stroke from about (297,215) up to (326,181). It is a line, not a streamer, and its base and tip are hard to tell apart.
Star placement is plausible and the orientation is right (pennant points up, hull sits low). The problem is the drawing language, not the placement.
